title: writer-pushed owned wake delivery for primary harnesses, independent of advanced autopilot
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-28/29 finished crew rounds sat unhandled for up to six hours because firstmate's waits were hand-made per round and lapsed whenever a turn ended without one (the captain: 'you have no watcher, it happens often'). kunchenguid/firstmate solves this by taking re-arming away from the model: a one-shot watcher, re-armed by the harness's own Stop hook, wakes the session on an actionable event. The captain approved this direction on 2026-09-29, and on the same day re-scoped it: watching is done by scripts, and this task bridges the project wake queue to the harness independently of the later T-141 autopilot and asked that it work for every primary harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others). Here the crew side is already uniform - every worker and reviewer round is run by fm-worker.sh/fm-review.sh, whatever the vendor, and emits the same events - so only the primary's wake path is per harness. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-137.json, is committed on this branch.

Writer-pushed contract (T-151; design section 15.7): crew launchers, board/server.ts and bin/fm-decide.sh append actionable records to project state/wake-queue and notify the session FIFO; T-141 is a future additional writer. External queues live under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/state, never engine state. Block on notifications with an owner-bound lifeline; no separate polling watcher or beacon. Preserve durable cursors, replay/deduplication and single-flight ownership. The recorded Claude Code 2.1.284 asyncRewake experiment established idle delivery there; other versions and harnesses require their own evidence. T-164 distinguishes native loading, enablement, exact trust, reload and actual delivery; a queue/ack receipt alone proves no model-visible wake.

Scheduled 2026-09-29 by the captain ('Hook全面取代也要排進去') right after T-151, no longer behind T-141: the push path stands on its own. Writers in this task are every event that needs firstmate today - a crew round ending (fm-worker.sh and fm-review.sh at their end: verdict, failure, lost), a captain decision (board, fm-decide.sh), a PR check finishing when fm already watches it - each appending to state/wake-queue and ringing the FIFO. With this merged, firstmate needs no hand-made waiter of any kind (the ops scripts' `until grep` loops are retired). T-141's autopilot, when it lands, is one more writer through the same call; nothing here waits for it.

Installing the hooks (firstmate ruling, 2026-09-29, after round 3): no harness config is committed - a round's sandbox cannot write .claude/ or .cursor/, and firstmate makes no commits. `fm hooks install [--harness claude|codex|cursor]` writes or merges the hook entries into each harness's local, uncommitted config for this repository (Claude Code: .claude/settings.local.json; Codex and Cursor: their documented local equivalents, named in docs/verification/supervision.md), idempotently, printing what it changed; `fm hooks uninstall` removes exactly those entries. `bin/fm-session.sh start` runs the install for the harness it detects, and reports installation separately from native loading, enablement, exact trusted command, required reload and verified delivery under T-164; never fabricate trust or bypass a refused command. Tests run install, a second install (no change), uninstall, and a merge into an existing settings file, in a temp directory. docs/verification/supervision.md is written by the round: Claude Code with the facts firstmate measured on 2026-09-29 (2.1.284: idle wake via asyncRewake exit 2; a plain hook orphaned on SIGKILL and stealing the next wake; the owner watch), Codex and Cursor marked unverified until firstmate records a live check after merge - and nothing claims an unverified path works.

The bridge blocks on writer-pushed wake notifications and its named owner's exit via T-151 lifelines. Durable project cursors ensure each actionable item is handled once; missing or uncertain ownership is reported honestly. No beacon is liveness evidence and no T-141 service is required for crew/decision/check-completion writers. The bridge never polls GitHub.

Zero tokens while idle: the harness hook parks on the wake queue inside its own process (a blocked read, not a model turn); the model runs only when a wake item arrives. No ScheduleWakeup, /loop or timed self-wake is used for watching.

Arming (bin/fm-watch-arm.sh): one owner-bound delivery cycle per session/project under a lock and generation. Repeated hooks attach to that cycle. Confirmed owner exit releases it; uncertain ownership is not permission to start a duplicate. Re-arm without losing durable queued wakes, using pushed notifications and lifelines rather than checking whether a PID/directory exists.

Per-harness delivery is recorded with exact version and live evidence in docs/verification/supervision.md. Preserve verified Claude asyncRewake and synchronous guard behavior. For Codex/Cursor, distinguish installed hooks, native loading and exact trust from actual delivery; a compatible shared app-server turn/start path needs live verification. Without a verified idle-wake path, read queued work on the next turn and visibly report pending delivery; never claim that a foreground blocking call or a Stop hook can wake an idle model. Unsupported hooks are reported, with visible host/board notification as an observation fallback, not proof of model delivery.

Only the primary arms delivery: FM_IN_ROUND and worktree identity prevent crew rounds from arming a primary hook. Outside-round crew launchers still publish completion wakes. Away-mode hook policy remains deferred until its task is approved.

Visible accountability: the board reports owned delivery-cycle state, queued versus delivered wakes, last reason and any coverage/delivery gap in en and zh-TW. No beacon-age substitute for liveness. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md keeps the rule that work is never left without supported scripted supervision and reports delivery limits honestly.

Tests (fail first; stubs answer as each harness does, taken from its docs or recorded payloads): each event kind wakes exactly once; progress is absorbed; two arms attach to one owned cycle; confirmed owner exit is handled and uncertain ownership retained; re-arm loses no durable wake; each harness hook's stop and wake contract; crew rounds never arm, while launchers publish their completion. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate, plus the recorded live verification per harness. Workers do not run the suites themselves.
